actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Seed of the environment's random generator
inputs.name: seed

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

facts.text: The action space is Box(0, 1, (4,)): four motor commands between zero and one
The observation is [roll, pitch, wrapped yaw, roll rate, pitch rate, yaw rate] as a float array
The observation space is Box(0, 1, (6,)), which does not bound the state; the source carries a TODO to fix it
A step clips the action to [0, 1], sets each desired rotor speed to sqrt(action) times max_rotor_speed, integrates one 0.02 s step and returns the state, reward, done and info
The default maximum rotor speed is 500.0
Rotor speeds approach the desired speed with gamma = 1 - 0.5**(dt / rotor_speed_half_time) and are clamped at zero
The attitude reward is -angle_factor * angle_error - angvel_factor * sum(angular_velocity^2), with angle_error = pitch^2 + roll^2 + yaw^2
The environment uses AttitudeReward(1.0, attitude_error_transform=np.sqrt), so the angle term is the square root of the squared angle error
The target band is 1 degree and the in-target bonus is 0.5
The bonus is added separately for roll, pitch and yaw when each absolute error is below the target
Roll and pitch are clipped at pi/4; when clipping happens the reward is reduced by the boundary penalty 1.0
A reset randomises roll and pitch within 20 degrees and the angular velocity within 2.0, sets yaw uniformly in [-0.3, 0.3], places the copter at altitude 1 and halves the yaw rate
The environment step never signals done: _step_copter always returns False
The environment id is registered with max_episode_steps=500, so gym.make wraps it in a 500-step TimeLimit
The legacy seed() calls gym.utils.seeding.np_random and returns [seed]
Body angular velocity is mapped to Euler-angle rates through the 3x3 matrix of the roll and pitch angles

determinism.notes: cap.world.reset.v1 with a seed, or a seed set by cap.world.seed.v1, makes the fake repeat a trajectory for the same actions; the fake draws initial states with Python's random.Random and upstream with numpy's generator, so a seed gives different trajectories on the two

gaps: rotational rigid-body dynamics only: positions and linear velocities are not simulated (the upstream environment fixes them each step, attitude_env.py:27); there are no contacts, no aerodynamic model and no ground or collision model

the rotor speeds approach the desired speed with a first-order lag (dynamics.py:86-90); no sensor or noise model is present, and the physical parameters are the upstream CopterParams defaults (copter.py:8-20)

the fake backend re-implements the equations in pure Python floats and draws initial states with Python's random.Random, not numpy's generator; it was not compared with the upstream environment (gym and numpy were not installed where the gate ran), so trajectories can differ
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0 and clock lockstep, so only step calls advance simulated time by the 20 ms integration step
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state or set_state
the observation space is the upstream Box(0, 1, (6,)), which does not bound the actual state (the upstream TODO at attitude_env.py:8); observations are published as numbers, not checked against it
the 500-step truncation comes from the registration's TimeLimit and is applied directly by the fake; the upstream TimeLimit wrapper is not present when the fake object is served

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
